The *Nandamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 11), translated as "Exposition of the Questions of the Student Nanda," is an exegetical canonical treatise located in the *Cūḷaniddesa* section of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Operating as an extensive commentary on the root verses of the *Nandamāṇavapucchā* (Snp 5.8) from the Pārāyanavagga of the *Suttanipāta*, the text provides word-by-word glosses and stock doctrinal expositions typical of the Niddesa literature [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records two modern translations of the text in two languages [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies curated passage-level parallels between the text and several canonical and post-canonical works, including the *Suddhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 4), *Pasūrasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 8), *Guhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 2), the *Milindapañha* (Mil 7.8.7, *Issāsaṅgapañha*), and the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 3.9, *Vipassanākathā*), in addition to a resembling parallel with the *Ajitamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 5) [SuttaCentral]. The text is also noted in connection with multiple discourses and treatises, notably its root verses in the *Nandamāṇavapucchā* (Snp 5.8), *Pucchā* (Cnd 2), the *Chandarāgasutta* (SN 22.25 and SN 23.9; SA 77), the *Padhāna Sutta* (Snp 3.2), and sections of the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 11, Mnd 13) [SuttaCentral].

Automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates 3,558 matching passages shared with 111 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest Pali reuse partners are other Niddesa treatises, including the *Māgaṇḍiyasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 9, sharing over 20,000 characters), *Puṇṇakamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 7), *Mahābyūhasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 13), and its underlying base text *Nandamāṇavapucchā* (Snp 5.8, sharing 118 matches, such as §24.7–28.1 with Snp §2.4–5.1) [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus aligns passages with Sanskrit and Tibetan works, including high-scoring alignments with the Sanskrit *Mahāvastu-avadāna* (§10.2_4 ↔ §12486) and *Lalitavistara*, the Tibetan *Buddhānusmṛtiṭīkā* (D3987) and *Lalitavistara* (D0095), and the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) [DharmaNexus].
